name: Bunny chow
summary: Quarter loaves of white bread hollowed out and filled with a spicy Durban sugar-bean and potato curry, topped with their own bread plug for mopping up the gravy.
about: Bunny chow was born in Durban's Indian community in the 1940s as a meal workers could carry and eat quickly: curry served in a hollowed loaf instead of with roti. The earliest bunnies were vegetarian, filled with sugar beans. It comes as a quarter, half or full loaf, is eaten with the fingers, and the soft bread plug, the 'virgin', is for dipping.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: medium, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and cinnamon and sizzle for 30 seconds, then add the onion and fry, stirring, until golden, 8–10 minutes.

Add the curry leaves, garlic, ginger and chillies and stir for 1 minute. Stir in the masala and turmeric with a splash of water and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, taking care not to burn the spices.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until they break down into a thick, oily gravy.
Add the potatoes and water, cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are almost tender.

Add the beans and salt and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until the potatoes are soft and the gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon. Some beans will break and thicken it further. Taste for salt and stir in the coriander.
While the curry simmers, mix the grated carrots, onion and vinegar with a pinch of salt and leave to stand.
Cut the loaf crossways into quarters. With a small knife, cut a square into the soft side of each quarter and pull out the crumb, leaving walls about 1.5 cm thick; keep the pulled-out plugs.
Ladle the hot curry into the bread to the brim, set a bread plug on top of each and serve at once, with the carrot salad on the side.
prepNote: The bean curry keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes well; fill the bread only when serving.
